subject: RapidCart - outlier latency & 5xx drain plan
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordane@rapidcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: RapidCart Ops <ops@rapidcart.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent huge latencies and rising 5xxs (started 11/4)

Marcus —

We're seeing repeated spikes in tail latency for our checkout completions (p99 jumping from ~1.2s to 18–30s) and a small but growing percentage of 5xx responses tied to the same time windows. Traffic pattern hasn't materially changed on our side. This started late Saturday evening (11/4) and we've observed multiple recurrence windows since.

Elena attached a small sample of traces and logs. We're escalating internally and RapidCart execs want visibility; can Redwood commit to an initial RCA timeline and mitigation steps?

Attachments: rc-traffic-sampler-logs.txt (text/plain)

Thanks,
Jordan
Head of Engineering, RapidCart
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordane@rapidcart.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent huge latencies and rising 5xxs (started 11/4)

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the traces. I've pulled in Hannah (runtime lead) and Monica (CS lead) to coordinate. Immediate plan:

1) We will run a focused telemetry snapshot across your production partition to capture queue depths, in-flight KV cache stats, and per-GPU concurrency metrics. Expect that within 90 minutes.
2) If we see backpressure-induced queueing, we'll temporarily lower concurrency caps for the busiest worker pools and enable aggressive KV-prefix caching for identical sessions to reduce token processing overhead.
3) We'll provide an initial incident brief to your execs within 3 hours with mitigations and a timeline for a more complete RCA.

Can you confirm the primary customer region (us-west vs us-east) and whether you rolled any client-side changes around midnight 11/4?

Marcus
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent huge latencies and rising 5xxs (started 11/4)

Looping internal runbook notes —

Observed pattern that often correlates to the p99 tail: transient worker pool saturation + KV cache misses when similar long contexts arrive in bursts. Key telemetry to grab now:
- per-worker active streams
- request size distribution (tokens) in offending windows
- kernel queue lengths and GC pauses on the host shim

If we confirm backlog, short-term levers: cap concurrency per-GPU to 70% of measured sustainable throughput, bias routing away from freshly-warmed hosts, and enable short-lived token-prefetch caching for similar session prefixes.

I'll take the first telemetry snapshot and attach cursory graphs to the exec brief.

—Hannah
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordane@rapidcart.com>
Cc: RapidCart Ops <ops@rapidcart.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Nov 2028 18:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent huge latencies and rising 5xxs (started 11/4)

Jordan —

Quick update and immediate asks:

What we did (15:00–17:30):
• Collected system snapshot for the windows 23:40–00:20 UTC on 11/04. Attached telemetry_snapshot.csv and a short log extract.
• Applied temporary per-GPU concurrency cap to the busiest pool (reduced to 70% throughput) at 17:05 PST.
• Bypassed two hosts that reported higher-than-normal kernel queue depth; traffic routed to warm pools.

Immediate effect: p99 in the sampled windows dropped from ~22s -> ~2.1s after caps/rerouting; 5xx rate decreased from 0.9% to 0.15% in the warm window.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Run a controlled warmup for the impacted pools overnight to reduce cold starts (Redwood) — timeline: 6–8 hours.
2) RapidCart to provide: sample payloads for the checkout flow that produce the long contexts (Elena).
3) Joint validation on Monday morning (11/6) at 10:00 PT for end-to-end test and post-mitigation telemetry.

We want to escalate to your execs with these concrete numbers and the draft playbook attached — please confirm you'd like us to include the numeric before/after in the note.

Marcus
[Attachments: telemetry_snapshot.csv, mutual_action_plan_rapidcart_v2.docx]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, VP Support <vp_support@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RapidCart — interim exec brief: outlier latency windows and mitigation status

Team —

Short executive summary for visibility:
• Incident window: recurring tail latency spikes beginning 2028-11-04 23:40 UTC tied to bursts of long-context checkout sessions.
• Impact: temporary p99 spikes up to ~30s and elevated 5xxs (peak ~1.2%); customer revenue impact estimated small but visible during peak windows.
• Immediate mitigations applied: per-GPU concurrency cap (70%), host reroute, and KV-prefix caching for similar sessions. Immediate p99 improvement observed (~22s -> ~2s).
• Next actions: joint replay test scheduled 2028-11-06 10:00 PT (confirmed), controlled warmup tonight, and a formal RCA due EOD 2028-11-08.

We're recommending a post-mortem focus on two contributing factors: request-size tail correlation with kernel queueing, and routing policy that steers freshly spun hosts into high-similarity traffic bursts. We're also recommending a change to rollout policy for long-context workloads to avoid simultaneous warm-up valleys.

If RapidCart would like a realtime bridge with Redwood engineering during Monday's replay, we can provide a bridge and a dedicated infra pager.

Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
